title: Resilience & messaging
subtitle: Handle timeouts, repeated requests, and duplicate messages.
description: Use bounded retries and idempotency, protect dependencies with circuit breakers, and understand message acknowledgements. Apply outbox and saga patterns across service boundaries.

lessons.title: Timeout, retry & idempotency
lessons.summary: Retries help transient failures only when repeating the operation is safe.
objectives: Use an idempotency key for uncertain POST outcomes.
keyPoints: A timeout does not prove the server failed to commit.
Bound retries with a total deadline, backoff, and jitter.
Store the operation and idempotency key atomically in shared storage.
practice: Retry order creation using the same key and payload.
Only one order is created, and reusing the key with a different payload is rejected.

exercises.prompt: Which conditions may justify an automatic retry, provided the operation is safe to repeat?
options: 503 Service Unavailable
A response read timeout
400 Bad Request
409 Conflict because stock is exhausted
exercises.explanation: Retry transient conditions, not invalid requests or business conflicts. Repeating a non-idempotent operation requires an idempotency strategy.

exercises.prompt: A client sends POST /orders and times out. What is definitely true?
options: The client does not know whether an order was created.
The order was definitely not created.
The order was definitely created.
The server is definitely down.
exercises.explanation: The response may be lost after a successful commit, so blindly retrying POST can create duplicates.

exercises.prompt: Configure a Resilience4j Retry instance named inventory with at most 3 attempts, a 200ms initial wait, and exponential backoff.
exercises.explanation: maxAttempts includes the first call. Exponential backoff increases delays; jitter helps avoid synchronized retry bursts.

lessons.title: Circuit breaker
lessons.summary: Stop calling a failing dependency temporarily so callers can fail quickly and the dependency can recover.
keyPoints: CLOSED records call results in a sliding window.
OPEN rejects calls without contacting the dependency.
HALF_OPEN permits probes to decide whether to close or reopen.
practice: Configure a circuit breaker and observe a failing Inventory dependency.
The circuit rejects calls while open and allows recovery probes later.

exercises.prompt: Order the circuit breaker cycle as a dependency fails and recovers.
items: CLOSED forwards calls and records their results.
Failure rate crosses the threshold after the minimum sample count.
The wait expires and the circuit enters HALF_OPEN.
Successful probes return the circuit to CLOSED.
exercises.explanation: HALF_OPEN probes recovery. Failed probes reopen the circuit and restart its wait.

exercises.prompt: What happens to a new Inventory call while the circuit is OPEN?
options: It is rejected immediately with CallNotPermittedException without contacting Inventory.
It is sent with a longer timeout.
It is queued until the circuit closes.
It automatically goes to another Inventory instance.
exercises.explanation: Failing fast frees caller resources and avoids repeatedly loading a dependency known to be failing.

exercises.prompt: Which Resilience4j property sets the minimum number of calls before calculating the failure rate?
exercises.hint: Look for the minimum sample-count property.
exercises.explanation: minimumNumberOfCalls prevents a tiny sample from opening the circuit too early.

lessons.title: Event, acknowledgement & duplicates
lessons.summary: Publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements protect different stages of message delivery. Consumers still need to tolerate duplicates.
objectives: Distinguish publisher confirm from consumer acknowledgement.
keyPoints: Confirm establishes broker acceptance; ack reports completion of consumption.
Acknowledging before work can lose it; acknowledging afterward can lead to redelivery.
Use idempotent consumers and a bounded retry/dead-letter policy.
practice: Send the same notification event twice and record processed IDs.
Only one notification is recorded for that event ID.

exercises.prompt: A consumer acknowledges before sending email, then crashes during delivery. What can happen?
options: The broker has removed the message, so the email may never be sent.
The broker necessarily resends the message.
The email is necessarily sent twice.
Nothing.
exercises.explanation: Acknowledging after successful processing trades loss risk for duplicate risk, which the consumer can address with idempotency.

exercises.prompt: Skip an event if processed.existsById(event.id()) is true; otherwise send the notification and store its ID.
exercises.explanation: A unique ID constraint handles competing consumers. External side effects still need provider-side idempotency to cover a crash between sending and recording.

lessons.title: Outbox, saga & eventual consistency
lessons.summary: Outbox writes business data and an event atomically. A saga coordinates local transactions and compensations across services.
objectives: Persist an event in the same transaction as the order.
Order compensating actions for a failed workflow.
keyPoints: A database commit cannot automatically commit a separate broker publish.
An outbox relay publishes stored events and may deliver duplicates.
Compensation is a new business operation, not a distributed database rollback.
practice: Write an order and outbox record in one transaction, then publish through a relay.
The event remains available if the broker fails and consumers can handle redelivery.

exercises.prompt: An order commits, but publishing OrderCreated fails because the broker is down. What is the problem?
options: The order exists but other services never receive its event.
The database automatically rolls back.
The broker automatically reads the event from the database.
Retries are guaranteed to fix it without stored state.
exercises.explanation: This is a dual write. Outbox stores the event with the order so a relay can publish it after recovery.

exercises.prompt: Payment fails after stock is reserved. Put the saga and its compensations in order.
items: Inventory releases the reservation as compensation.
Mark the order CANCELLED as compensation.
exercises.explanation: Compensations undo business effects of completed steps in reverse order.

exercises.prompt: Within the Transactional method, save the order and an outbox event together. Do not publish directly to the broker.
checks: Do not publish directly to the broker
exercises.explanation: The order and outbox record commit or roll back together. A separate relay handles broker delivery.
